site.name: shopify
site.summary: shopify-clone Clone of the Shopify marketing → trial → admin funnel. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: hero ("Your business starts with Shopify" + email signup input), product features, customer success stories, customer logos, footer | | `pricing.html` | Plan comparison: Basic / Shopify / Advanced three tiers, monthly / yearly toggle, feature comparison table, FAQ | | `free-trial.html` | Trial landing page: 3-step intro to the trial flow, value props restated, large "Start free trial" button |

run_plan.goal: Explore and critique the Shopify marketing-to-trial-to-admin funnel end to end, with primary focus on the free-trial onboarding flow and secondary coverage of pricing, resources, help, login, and sales-contact paths across desktop and mobile.
run_plan.summary: Begin on the marketing homepage and validate the main conversion entry points, especially the hero email/signup CTA and repeated trial calls to action. Then drive deeply through the multi-step free-trial form, including forward progress, skip behavior, and completion to the "Your store is ready!" state. After the core funnel, cover adjacent decision-support and recovery paths on pricing, help, resources, admin login, and sales pages, and finish by repeating the highest-value journey plus navigation/tap-target checks on mobile.
assumptions: The primary journey is marketing homepage or pricing/resources entry points into free-trial onboarding, ending in a ready-store/admin-like success state.

free-trial-form.html appears to be a scripted multi-step onboarding flow with intermediate questions, account creation fields, and a final success state even though only limited controls were exposed in prescan.
admin.html and sales.html likely use client-side success/error states because headings include success messages despite the prescan landing on the initial form views.
Some top-nav and footer links point to '#' placeholders, so exploration should prioritize real HTML destinations over dead-end links.
Mobile risk is elevated because multiple nav/footer links were flagged as undersized tap targets in prescan.
risk_hotspots: index.html hero email field + Start free trial button: validate whether email capture is required, optional, or ignored before navigation
index.html FAQ accordion buttons: confirm expand/collapse behavior and content visibility
free-trial-form.html multi-step onboarding: risk of hidden validation, skipped states, broken progression, and unclear persistence between steps
free-trial-form.html Skip all control: important recovery/shortcut path called out in page copy
free-trial-form.html Create your Shopify account step: validate required fields, inline errors, and transition to 'Your store is ready!'
admin.html login form: test required-field behavior, store URL formatting, and alternate social login buttons presence/state
sales.html contact form: prescan reports missing_input_label warnings, so inspect labeling, keyboard focus, and select controls carefully
pricing.html monthly/yearly toggle: verify that prices and plan messaging actually update
pricing.html plan CTAs and Contact sales path: ensure self-serve vs enterprise branching is clear
help-trial.html search input and on-page anchor navigation: validate discoverability and internal navigation behavior
Top navigation and footer links across marketing pages: many small tap targets suggest mobile usability issues

phases.title: Homepage conversion entry and content discovery
phases.objective: Validate the main marketing landing page as a starting point into the trial funnel and inspect the most visible conversion/support interactions.
key_checks: Use the hero email input and Start free trial submit button to see whether submission routes into onboarding and whether blank vs populated input changes behavior
Compare the top-nav Start free trial link with the hero CTA destination and consistency
Open at least the visible FAQ accordion items on the homepage and confirm expand/collapse usability
Check whether footer support links route correctly to help-trial.html and free-trial.html
Note whether free-trial.html is materially distinct from index.html or effectively duplicate content
exit_criteria: Primary homepage CTA path into free-trial-form.html is confirmed via at least one working entry point
At least two FAQ items are expanded and observed
Duplicate-or-distinct relationship between index.html and free-trial.html is established

phases.title: Deep free-trial onboarding walkthrough
phases.objective: Exercise the core onboarding funnel thoroughly, covering guided setup, skip behavior, validation, and completion.
key_checks: Progress through the 'What are you planning to sell?' step and observe selection requirements before Next
Advance through 'Where would you like to sell?' and 'Where is your business located?' states, confirming transitions and back/continuation behavior if available
Use 'Skip all' to test the alternate fast-path and verify where it rejoins the flow
At the 'Create your Shopify account' step, test empty submission, partially completed submission, and a valid completion path if possible
Confirm the final 'Your store is ready!' state appears and document any success CTA or destination offered afterward
exit_criteria: Both a normal progression path and Skip-all path have been attempted or their availability limits clearly established
At least one validation behavior is observed on account creation or earlier required steps
The final success state is reached or a blocker is documented with specific failing step/control

phases.title: Decision support and enterprise branching
phases.objective: Validate plan comparison and the branch from self-serve pricing into enterprise sales contact.
key_checks: Toggle Pay monthly vs Pay yearly and verify displayed pricing changes for Basic/Grow/Advanced plans
Inspect plan card CTAs, especially Start free trial for self-serve plans and Contact sales for Plus
Open at least one pricing FAQ item and compare messaging against homepage trial/pricing claims
Follow the Contact sales path into sales.html and complete the form with the available text/select fields
Test sales form required-field behavior, select menus, and success acknowledgement state
exit_criteria: Pricing toggle behavior is confirmed as functional or nonfunctional
Enterprise branch to sales.html is exercised
Sales form is submitted successfully or validation failure points are captured

phases.title: Help, resources, and recovery journeys
phases.objective: Assess whether support and educational pages help users recover from uncertainty and re-enter the trial funnel.
key_checks: On help-trial.html, use the on-page table-of-contents links to jump among sections and confirm anchors work
Try the help search input to determine whether it accepts interaction and whether results/navigation occur
Follow the 'sign up for a free trial' help link back into the onboarding path
On resources.html, inspect key resource cards, especially Shopify Help Center, and confirm whether they navigate internally or externally within the local clone
Use the resources page trial CTA and compare its destination/behavior with homepage and pricing CTAs
exit_criteria: At least one support-driven re-entry into the free-trial funnel is confirmed
Help page anchor navigation is verified
Resources page CTA behavior is compared with other trial entry points

phases.title: Admin login and mobile critical-path verification
phases.objective: Probe the login experience and repeat the most important funnel checks under mobile constraints.
key_checks: On admin.html, test blank and populated login attempts using store URL, email, and password fields
Inspect 'Forgot password?' and the Apple/Google/Facebook buttons for visible affordance and behavior
Repeat on mobile: top-nav access, homepage hero CTA, and at least the first onboarding step on free-trial-form.html
Repeat on mobile: pricing toggle and one plan CTA
Pay special attention to previously flagged small tap targets in nav/footer and any overlap, clipping, or hard-to-tap controls
exit_criteria: Admin login form behavior is characterized, including whether any success/error state appears
Critical trial entry and first onboarding interaction are completed on mobile
At least one concrete mobile tap-target or layout issue is confirmed or ruled out on the key pages

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 8 known HTML pages, with deepest interaction on free-trial-form.html, pricing.html, admin.html, help-trial.html, and sales.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the main visible controls on each key page: homepage/email CTA and FAQs, onboarding progression and Skip all, pricing monthly/yearly toggle and plan CTAs, help anchors/search, login fields/social buttons, and sales form fields/selects/submit.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical funnel on mobile for index.html -> free-trial-form.html first step, plus pricing toggle/CTA and a quick nav/footer tap-target audit on pages already flagged with small targets.

notes: Do not spend much time on '#' placeholder links unless they unexpectedly open menus or reveal content.
Because free-trial.html appears very similar to index.html in prescan, treat it as a confirmation page rather than a separate deep dive unless execution shows meaningful differences.
If scripted states are hidden until interaction, prioritize reaching them over broad clicking on low-value footer links.

observation.visible_text: Shopify Solutions Pricing Resources Log in Start free trial Your business starts with Shopify Start for free, keep building for £1/month. Plus, earn up to £7,000 in credits as you sell. Start free trial You agree to receive Shopify marketing emails. Allbirds Gymshark Brooklinen Leesa Kylie Cosmetics Crate & Barrel Monos CUSTOMIZABLE THEMES Create a stunning store in seconds Pre-built designs make it fast and easy to kickstart your brand. Total sales £700,000 +£7,000 GET REWARDED Your plan can pay for itself Turn sales into savings with 1% back as subscription credits. MEET SIDEKICK Level up with our AI assistant With millions of AI tokens to use with our built-in assistant, you can grow without limits. Hey Arda, How can I help? Ask Sidekick anything about your store... Shop Pay Klarna Mastercard Visa ALL-IN-ONE Getting stuff done? Done. Shopify handles everything from secure payments to marketing and hardware. "We've tripled in size since we first started on Shopify. It gives us the tools we need to keep pushing forward." — Shopify Merchant No risk, all rewards. Try Shopify for £1/month. Plus, earn up to £7,000 in credits as you sell. Start free trial You agree to receive Shopify marketing emails. Questions? What is Shopify and how does it work? Shopify is a complete commerce platform that lets you start, grow, and manage a business. With Shopify, you can build an online store, manage sales, market to customers, and accept payments in digital and physical locations. How much does Shopify cost? Try Shopify free for 3 days, no credit card required. After your trial expires, choose a pricing plan that suits the size and stage of your business. Can I use my own domain name with Shopify? Yes, you can use your own domain name with Shopify. If you have an existing domain name, you can connect it to Shopify from your store's admin. If you don't have a domain name yet, you can either buy one through Shopify or a third-party provider. Do I need to be a designer or developer to use Shopify? No, you don't need to be a designer or developer to use Shopify. Signing up for Shopify allows you to use pre-built themes, drag-and-drop editors, and AI tools to create your store without any coding knowledge. observation.title: Trying Shopify with a free trial – Shopify Help Center
observation.visible_text: Shopify Help Center ON THIS PAGE Available plans for trial Initiate the free trial Setting up your store Making the most of your trial Choosing a paid plan Trial period length Promotional pricing Deactivating your store Troubleshooting Trying Shopify with a free trial To explore Shopify before committing to an active monthly plan, you can sign up for a free trial. Your free trial begins when you first sign up, not when you start working on your store. Available plans for trial The free trial allows you to test out various Shopify plans, including: Starter Basic Grow Advanced Shopify Retail Initiate the free trial Visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Answer a set of questions tailored to your business needs, or choose Skip All. Specify your business location. Create a Shopify account to start your free trial. Setting up your store during the free trial When you open a store on a free trial, your store initially has either a storefront password or an inactive checkout. To allow customers to purchase products, you can either remove the storefront password, or you can activate your online store checkout by choosing a paid plan. To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider. You won't lose any work completed on your store during the free trial when you select a paid plan. Making the most of your free trial During your free trial period, you have the opportunity to set up your store and explore its features. Here are some ways to maximize your trial experience: Add products: Populate your store with a few products and ensure their product details are displayed correctly on your online store. Create collections: Organize your products by creating collections to enhance the shopping experience for your customers. Explore settings: Familiarize yourself with the Settings page in your Shopify admin to configure taxes, shipping, and other sales channels. Set up payments: Configure Shopify Payments or verify that your preferred third-party payment provider is supported by Shopify. Visit the theme and app store: Visit the Shopify Theme Store and the Shopify App Store to discover themes and apps that can enhance your store's functionality and appearance. Choosing a paid plan When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan. Any progress you made during your free trial, including products added, designs made, and settings adjusted are retained when you choose a paid plan. Review the following considerations before choosing a paid plan: Store activation: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout is activated. Trial expiry: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan. Cancellation: If you decide to cancel your Shopify account during the free trial without selecting a pricing plan, then no action is required, and your account is frozen. Billing cycle affects the monthly price: When selecting a plan, monthly billing and annual billing have different total costs. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate. Charges incurred during your free trial If you add apps to your Shopify store during your free trial period, then any app-related charges are included on your next invoice. Switching between plans during your free trial You can switch between Shopify plans during your free trial. The new plan takes effect immediately, but you aren't charged until your free trial period ends. Free trial period length and details The length of your free trial can vary based on different factors. To find out the current trial length and any promotional offers available, visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Note: It's not possible to extend the duration of your free trial period. If you decide to upgrade to a paid plan within your free trial period, then charges wi

observation.title: Trying Shopify with a free trial – Shopify Help Center
observation.visible_text: Shopify Help Center ON THIS PAGE Available plans for trial Initiate the free trial Setting up your store Making the most of your trial Choosing a paid plan Trial period length Promotional pricing Deactivating your store Troubleshooting Trying Shopify with a free trial To explore Shopify before committing to an active monthly plan, you can sign up for a free trial. Your free trial begins when you first sign up, not when you start working on your store. Available plans for trial The free trial allows you to test out various Shopify plans, including: Starter Basic Grow Advanced Shopify Retail Initiate the free trial Visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Answer a set of questions tailored to your business needs, or choose Skip All. Specify your business location. Create a Shopify account to start your free trial. Setting up your store during the free trial When you open a store on a free trial, your store initially has either a storefront password or an inactive checkout. To allow customers to purchase products, you can either remove the storefront password, or you can activate your online store checkout by choosing a paid plan. To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider. You won't lose any work completed on your store during the free trial when you select a paid plan. Making the most of your free trial During your free trial period, you have the opportunity to set up your store and explore its features. Here are some ways to maximize your trial experience: Add products: Populate your store with a few products and ensure their product details are displayed correctly on your online store. Create collections: Organize your products by creating collections to enhance the shopping experience for your customers. Explore settings: Familiarize yourself with the Settings page in your Shopify admin to configure taxes, shipping, and other sales channels. Set up payments: Configure Shopify Payments or verify that your preferred third-party payment provider is supported by Shopify. Visit the theme and app store: Visit the Shopify Theme Store and the Shopify App Store to discover themes and apps that can enhance your store's functionality and appearance. Choosing a paid plan When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan. Any progress you made during your free trial, including products added, designs made, and settings adjusted are retained when you choose a paid plan. Review the following considerations before choosing a paid plan: Store activation: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout is activated. Trial expiry: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan. Cancellation: If you decide to cancel your Shopify account during the free trial without selecting a pricing plan, then no action is required, and your account is frozen. Billing cycle affects the monthly price: When selecting a plan, monthly billing and annual billing have different total costs. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate. Charges incurred during your free trial If you add apps to your Shopify store during your free trial period, then any app-related charges are included on your next invoice. Switching between plans during your free trial You can switch between Shopify plans during your free trial. The new plan takes effect immediately, but you aren't charged until your free trial period ends. Free trial period length and details The length of your free trial can vary based on different factors. To find out the current trial length and any promotional offers available, visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Note: It's not possible to extend the duration of your free trial period. If you decide to upgrade to a paid plan within your free trial period, then charges wi

dom_summary.visible_text: Shopify Help Center ON THIS PAGE Available plans for trial Initiate the free trial Setting up your store Making the most of your trial Choosing a paid plan Trial period length Promotional pricing Deactivating your store Troubleshooting Trying Shopify with a free trial To explore Shopify before committing to an active monthly plan, you can sign up for a free trial. Your free trial begins when you first sign up, not when you start working on your store. Available plans for trial The free trial allows you to test out various Shopify plans, including: Starter Basic Grow Advanced Shopify Retail Initiate the free trial Visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Answer a set of questions tailored to your business needs, or choose Skip All. Specify your business location. Create a Shopify account to start your free trial. Setting up your store during the free trial When you open a store on a free trial, your store initially has either a storefront password or an inactive checkout. To allow customers to purchase products, you can either remove the storefront password, or you can activate your online store checkout by choosing a paid plan. To sell and accept orders during your free trial, you need to set up a payment provider. You won't lose any work completed on your store during the free trial when you select a paid plan. Making the most of your free trial During your free trial period, you have the opportunity to set up your store and explore its features. Here are some ways to maximize your trial experience: Add products: Populate your store with a few products and ensure their product details are displayed correctly on your online store. Create collections: Organize your products by creating collections to enhance the shopping experience for your customers. Explore settings: Familiarize yourself with the Settings page in your Shopify admin to configure taxes, shipping, and other sales channels. Set up payments: Configure Shopify Payments or verify that your preferred third-party payment provider is supported by Shopify. Visit the theme and app store: Visit the Shopify Theme Store and the Shopify App Store to discover themes and apps that can enhance your store's functionality and appearance. Choosing a paid plan When you're ready to start selling products, you need to select a paid plan. Any progress you made during your free trial, including products added, designs made, and settings adjusted are retained when you choose a paid plan. Review the following considerations before choosing a paid plan: Store activation: After you choose a paid plan, your online store's checkout is activated. Trial expiry: If you don't select a monthly plan at the end of your free trial, then your store is paused until you choose a paid plan. Cancellation: If you decide to cancel your Shopify account during the free trial without selecting a pricing plan, then no action is required, and your account is frozen. Billing cycle affects the monthly price: When selecting a plan, monthly billing and annual billing have different total costs. Annual billing charges the full year upfront and presents a lower effective monthly rate. Charges incurred during your free trial If you add apps to your Shopify store during your free trial period, then any app-related charges are included on your next invoice. Switching between plans during your free trial You can switch between Shopify plans during your free trial. The new plan takes effect immediately, but you aren't charged until your free trial period ends. Free trial period length and details The length of your free trial can vary based on different factors. To find out the current trial length and any promotional offers available, visit the free trial page, enter your email address, and then click Start free trial. Shopify is a complete commerce platform that lets you start, grow, and manage a business. With Shopify, you can build an online store, manage sales, market to customers, and accept payments in digital and physical locations. How much does Shopify cost? Try Shopify free for 3 days, no credit card required. After your trial expires, choose a pricing plan that suits the size and stage of your business. Can I use my own domain name with Shopify? Yes, you can use your own domain name with Shopify. If you have an existing domain name, you can connect it to Shopify from your store's admin. If you don't have a domain name yet, you can either buy one through Shopify or a third-party provider. Do I need to be a designer or developer to use Shopify? No, you don't need to be a designer or developer to use Shopify. Signing up for Shopify allows you to use pre-built themes, drag-and-drop editors, and AI tools to create your store without any coding knowledge. Allbirds Gymshark Brooklinen Patagonia Crate & Barrel Frequently asked questions What is Shopify and how does it work? Shopify is a complete commerce platform that lets you start, grow, and manage a business. You can use Shopify to build an online store, manage sales, market to customers, and accept payments in digital and physical locations. How much does Shopify cost? Shopify plans start at £25/month for Basic. You can try any plan free for 3 days, then enjoy £1/month for your first 3 months. No credit card required to start. How long are your contracts? Shopify plans are month-to-month by default. You can also choose annual billing for a discount. There are no long-term contracts — you can cancel at any time. Can I cancel my account at any time? Yes, you can cancel your Shopify account at any time. If you cancel during your free trial, you won't be charged. If you cancel after selecting a plan, your store will remain active until the end of your current billing period. Can I change my plan later on? Yes, you can upgrade or downgrade your plan at any time from your Shopify admin. Changes take effect immediately, and any price differences are prorated. Are there third-party transaction fees? If you use Shopify Payments, there are no additional transaction fees. If you use a third-party payment provider, additional fees of 2%, 1%, or 0.6% apply depending on your plan (Basic, Grow, or Advanced). Shopify plans start at £25/month for Basic. You can try any plan free for 3 days, then enjoy £1/month for your first 3 months. No credit card required to start. How long are your contracts? Shopify plans are month-to-month by default. You can also choose annual billing for a discount. There are no long-term contracts — you can cancel at any time. Can I cancel my account at any time? Yes, you can cancel your Shopify account at any time. If you cancel during your free trial, you won't be charged. If you cancel after selecting a plan, your store will remain active until the end of your current billing period. Can I change my plan later on? Yes, you can upgrade or downgrade your plan at any time from your Shopify admin. Changes take effect immediately, and any price differences are prorated. Are there third-party transaction fees? If you use Shopify Payments, there are no additional transaction fees. If you use a third-party payment provider, additional fees of 2%, 1%, or 0.6% apply depending on your plan (Basic, Grow, or Advanced).
